### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), reindexSource (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 517e4153c6e8e68cd194c3a2321476da9bb9b332` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0240378548e98d5fe7b276005a1c411963f38033` — the merge of head `9e24b96c22ad3f8ea1707543939338489f7af2a5` into base `517e4153c6e8e68cd194c3a2321476da9bb9b332`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0240378548e98d5fe7b276005a1c411963f38033 && git checkout 0240378548e98d5fe7b276005a1c411963f38033
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 517e4153c6e8e68cd194c3a2321476da9bb9b332 9e24b96c22ad3f8ea1707543939338489f7af2a5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 517e4153c6e8e68cd194c3a2321476da9bb9b332 && git merge --no-ff 9e24b96c22ad3f8ea1707543939338489f7af2a5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 517e4153c6e8e68cd194c3a2321476da9bb9b332
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 517e4153c6e8e68cd194c3a2321476da9bb9b332` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — REWORK · L1 · head `99518e665ef655150b07d968de1a8f97975abba7` · 2026-11-24T22:08Z

Requested by zone a4-K (7145688334) for card #36992.

Delivered and correct: every card item is in (`knowledge-service.ts`); the sort is explicit (`orderBy` id asc on every page) and the test double refuses its absence; the cursor keeps the id's own type and the no-advance guard checks equality only, never a JS comparison that could disagree with a database collation; `where` composes with `$and` exactly as the #36991 sync does; the system context goes in the contract's trailing argument; the two promise chains are separate maps, so no deadlock; `where`, `orderBy`, `limit` and `count` all push down to the engine (Prime Directive 5); a `limit` of 150 reads 100 then 50 with no extra read; no result field and no adapter contract member added. The three ablations re-derive as stated. `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. Check-runs: 36 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed. K: 6.

M1 (must-fix) — `if (rows.length < want) break;` (`knowledge-service.ts` ~311) ends the walk with `ok:true` whenever a page comes back short. `find` does not promise `min(limit, remaining)` rows: an `afterFind` handler may replace the result (`packages/objectql/src/engine-find.ts` ~654-673; pinned in `engine-find-hook-result-shape.test.ts`), so one dropped row silently leaves every later row out of the index — a regression from the single unbounded read this replaces. Fix: end only on an empty page or at the cap; pin a page that returns 99 of a full 100 with every later row still upserted; ablate by restoring the break; the 101-row test then expects three reads.
S1 (should-fix) — the lock claim (`knowledge-service.ts` ~199-203 and the changeset's "One reindex per source" bullet: "pages never interleave (the same promise chain as the record sync)") overstates it: walks share `chainAfter`, not the record-sync chain, and record events never wait for a walk, so a row deleted or updated between a page's read and its upsert is written back from the older read (a deleted row becomes a ghost document until the purge, #37096). The race predates this PR and paging narrows it. Reword to what is enforced: same-source walks wait for each other; record events do not wait; name #37096.
S2 (should-fix) — the "reindex repairs bulk deletes" drift is carried on the wrong card and has three sites: `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` ~411, the rolled-back-insert passage ~386-392, and the runtime warning in `knowledge-service-plugin.ts` ~282. The purge is #37096 (epic row 2), not the ADR #37001. Either trim ~411 here (inside the claimed surface) or record all three sites on #37096 — not on #37001.

Nits: N1 the new describe has 17 cases, not 16 (body and report); N2 `recordToDocument` runs outside the page's try, and `(err as Error).message` reads `undefined` for a thrown non-Error — bring both under the `ok:false` path; N3 normalise `limit` (floor, clamp; a negative or NaN now returns a silent `ok:true, 0`); N4 one case with numeric ids 1..150.

The zone's two questions: (a) "checked once" for the SQL cursor order is enough — no follow-up card; add one line on #37100 asking for a reindex-over-a-real-driver case (PostgreSQL non-C collation is where it can differ). (b) see S2.

Delta L1 on the new head.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · L1 · head `9e24b96c22ad3f8ea1707543939338489f7af2a5` · 2026-11-24T22:48Z

Delta L1 for card #36992 over the REWORK at `99518e665e` (7145865808), requested by zone a4-K (7146650869).

- **M1: closed.** Only an empty page ends the walk (the short-page `break` is gone, with a comment naming why: an `afterFind` hook may drop rows); a walk now ends on an empty page or the cap. Pinned: a page that lost a row to a hook does not stop the walk; the ablation restoring the break turns 3 cases red.
- **S1: closed.** The doc comment says what is enforced: same-source walks wait for each other (a per-source `chainAfter` chain), record events do not wait for a walk, and a row changed between a page's read and its upsert is written back from the older read — a deleted row's document stays as a ghost until the purge, #37096.
- **S2: closed.** No sentence says a reindex removes documents: `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` (the predicate-write passage and the rollback passage) and the runtime warning in `knowledge-service-plugin.ts` now say a reindex refreshes rows that still exist and match and removes none; the rest waits for #37096.
- **N1–N4: done.** The case count is corrected; `recordToDocument` runs under the page's `ok:false` path and a thrown non-Error is reported by its text (`errorText`), both pinned; `limit` is floored when fractional and refused with `ok:false` when negative or non-finite (pinned); numeric ids 1..150 page in numeric order.
- **The previous head's three reds** (`6ffdf21e`): Test Core 9/10 was this PR's (the legacy reindex doubles returned the same rows each page, now answering an empty next page); the other two were aggregates cancelled by the new push.
- **Gates.** Check-runs at this head: 41 success, 17 expected skip, 0 failed, 1 pending — the PR-body check re-triggered by the body edit; the zone confirms it green before landing. Landing K: 10.
- No must-fix, no should-fix. The zone lands it once that check is green.
